table.caption: Which level of government decides each matter in two invented countries (invented data for practice)
rows: The national parliament, by passing a law
The constitution, which needs the provinces to agree to change it

forms-of-governance-s2.title: The Tenth Amendment to the US Constitution (1791)
forms-of-governance-s2.text:
"The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people."

Tenth Amendment to the Constitution of the United States, ratified 1791. "Delegated" means handed over; "reserved" means kept.

items.q: Which form of government does Country Q have?
options: Federal
Unitary, run from the capital
Autonomous
Stateless

why.correct: In Country Q, schools, police and some taxes belong to the provinces, and the constitution protects those powers: a federal state.
options: Right: Its provinces have their own powers, set out in a constitution.
In a unitary state, the national government decides most matters, as in Country P.
An autonomous region is a part of a state, not a whole system of government.
Stateless describes a nation with no state.

items.q: Which row of the table best shows that Country P is a unitary state?
options: Army and money
Income tax and who collects it
Police and courts in each province
Who can change these powers

why.correct: In a unitary state, the national government holds final power and can give or take powers from regions by ordinary law. That is what the last row shows for Country P.
options: Both countries give these to the national government.
This row shows that Country Q shares taxes; it does not show who holds final power in P.
This row matters, but the strongest sign is who can change the powers.
Right: The national parliament alone can change who decides what.

items.q: A family moves from one province of Country Q to another. Based on the table, what is most likely to change for them?
options: The money they use to buy food and pay rent
The army that defends them
What their children are taught at school
Whether they pay any national income tax

why.correct: In a federal state, laws differ from one subnational unit to the next for the matters that belong to them, such as schools in Country Q.
options: Money is decided by the national government in both countries.
The army is national in both countries.
Right: Each province decides its own school lessons.
The national government taxes income in every province.

items.q: What does the table show about both countries?
options: Neither has a national government
Both have a national government that controls the army and money
Both let provinces decide what schools teach
Both need the provinces to agree before powers change

why.correct: Readers who score the exam report that students describe a federal state as if it had no national government. It does: power is shared between the national and the subnational levels.
options: Both have one; the first row shows it.
Right: A federal state still has a strong national level.
In Country P, the national government decides.
That is true of Country Q alone.

items.q: According to the passage, who keeps the powers that the Constitution does not give to the national government?
options: The states, or the people
The national government
The Supreme Court
Other countries

why.correct: The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states, or the people, every power the Constitution does not delegate to the national government.
options: Right: Powers not handed to the national government are kept by the states or the people.
The passage says these powers are reserved to the states.
The passage does not mention the courts.
The passage is about powers inside the United States.

items.q: Which form of government does the passage support?
options: A unitary state
A stateless nation
A nation-state
A federal state

why.correct: Dividing powers by a constitution between the national level and the states is the mark of a federal state.
options: A unitary state keeps final power at the national level.
A stateless nation has no state at all.
That term is about one nation in one state, not how power is shared.
Right: It divides powers between the national government and the states.

items.q: Because of the arrangement in the passage, which pattern would you expect to see across the United States?
options: One speed limit set for roads across the country
One national police force running each town
Laws such as minimum wages differ by state
A different money in each state

why.correct: Federal systems produce variety at the subnational scale: minimum wages, speed limits and school rules differ from state to state, while money and defense stay national.
options: States set most speed limits, so they differ.
Most policing is run by states and local governments.
Right: States use their reserved powers in different ways.
Money is a power the Constitution gives to the national government.
A state that shares power between national and state governments
A state in which the national government holds most power
A state made of one nation
A state that belongs to a group of states

why.correct: In a unitary state, power is concentrated in the national government, which can create, change or remove regional powers.
options: That is a federal state.
Right: Regions carry out national decisions and have only the powers the center gives them.
That is a nation-state; a unitary state may hold many nations.
That describes membership in an organization, not a form of government.

items.q: In France, the national government in Paris sets what is taught in schools across the country, and regions carry out national policies. What form of government does this suggest?
options: Unitary
Federal
Autonomous
Multistate

why.correct: France is a common example of a unitary state: power is centered in Paris.
options: Right: Power is concentrated at the national level, in the capital.
In a federal state, the regions would have their own protected powers over schools.
An autonomous region is a part of a state, not the state's system.
Multistate describes a nation spread across states.

items.q: India has hundreds of languages and is home to many peoples. Why might a federal system suit it?
options: A federal system makes people across India speak one language
A federal system removes the national government
A federal system is needed by any country with a large population
States can set some rules, such as languages, to fit local cultures

why.correct: Federal systems often suit large or culturally diverse states. In India, states were redrawn largely along language lines after 1956 and run many of their own affairs.
options: Indian states use many official languages.
India's national government stays in charge of defense and money.
China has a larger population and a unitary system.
Right: Sharing power lets different regions govern in their own ways inside one state.

items.q: Which statement correctly compares unitary and federal states?
options: Unitary states have no regions of any kind; federal states are split into regions
Unitary states are large; federal states are small
Both have a national government; federal ones also protect regional powers
Federal states have no national government; unitary states have one

why.correct: A compare speaks of both sides. Both forms have a national government; in a federal state the constitution also protects powers for regional governments.
options: Unitary states have regions too, but those carry out national decisions.
Small Switzerland is federal and large China is unitary.
Right: The difference is whether regional powers are protected by a constitution.
Federal states have a national government that runs defense and money.

items.q: Finland is a unitary state, but its Åland Islands, where most people speak Swedish, make many of their own laws. What does this show?
options: Finland is in fact a federal state
A unitary state can still have an autonomous region
The Åland Islands are an independent state
Swedish speakers form a stateless nation in Finland

why.correct: A unitary state can grant special powers to one region, often where a different nation or language group lives, without becoming federal.
options: One autonomous region does not make the whole state federal.
Right: Finland gives Åland special powers while keeping national control elsewhere.
Åland is part of Finland.
Swedish speakers have their own state, Sweden, next door.

items.q: Which are features of a federal state? Select all that apply.
options: A constitution divides powers between national and regional governments
Regional governments make some of their own laws
The national government can remove regional powers by passing an ordinary law
There is no national army

why.correct: In a federal state, a constitution shares power between a national government and regional governments, each with its own protected powers.
options: Right: This is the defining feature.
Right: For example, US states set their own minimum wages.
That describes a unitary state.
Federal states have national armies.

items.q: Place the levels of government in the United States, a federal state, from the largest area at the top to the smallest at the bottom.

model.title: Levels of government in the United States

slips.why: The United Nations is an organization of states, not a level of US government.
A federal state still has a national government above its states: the readers report this slip.

why.correct: National government (the whole country), then the 50 state governments, then county governments, then city and town governments.

items.q: Build a comparison of a unitary state and a federal state, with a real example of each.

why.correct: A compare speaks of both sides, with an example for each.

specific.model: In France, a unitary state, the national government in Paris decides most matters, whereas in Germany, a federal state, the states (Länder) run their own schools and police while the national government runs defense and money.

sideA.label: Unitary example
options: France, a unitary state, the national government in Paris decides most matters
France, a federal state, the regions decide most matters

why.1: France is a common example of a unitary state.

sideB.label: Federal example
options: Germany, a federal state, the states run their own schools and police while the national government runs defense and money
Germany, a federal state, there is no national government

why.1: A federal state still has a national government: say what it runs.
